facts.statement: Seeleyosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur found in Germany and possibly Russia.
facts.quote: Seeleyosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from Germany and possibly also Russia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Seeleyosaurus is a large, almost complete skeleton discovered in the Upper Lias formations of Württemberg, Germany.
facts.quote: The holotype is MB.R.1992, a large almost complete skeleton from the Upper Lias (Toarcian) Lias Group Formations of Württemberg, Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was purchased by the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart in August 1893.
facts.quote: It was offered for sale by Bernard Hauff and it was purchased by the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart in August 1893.

facts.statement: The original holotype skeleton was destroyed in 1945.
A second 3D-preserved specimen was originally designated as the holotype for the species S. holzmadensis.
facts.quote: A second specimen (SMNS 12039), preserved in 3D, was initially the holotype of S. holzmadensis.

facts.statement: A second specimen was discovered in a quarry between Holzmaden and Zell unter Aichelberg, intersecting a forty-centimeter-thick layer of Stinkstein chalk.
facts.quote: It was discovered within a chalkstone and shale quarry located between Holzmaden and Zell unter Aichelberg, and it intersected an extremely hard forty centimetres thick layer of Stinkstein chalk, which was deemed worthless.

facts.statement: The second specimen was discovered in November 1906 by fossil trader Bernhard Hauff.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered there in November 1906 by fossil trader Bernhard Hauff.

facts.statement: A fragmentary specimen of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris was identified from the Middle Jurassic of Siberia by Menner in 1992.
facts.quote: A fragmentary specimen of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris has also been identified from the Middle Jurassic of Siberia by Menner (1992).

facts.statement: Seeleyosaurus was first described as Plesiosaurus guilelmiimperatoris by Dames in 1895 before being moved to its own genus by White in 1940.
facts.quote: Seeleyosaurus was initially described as Plesiosaurus guilelmiimperatoris by Dames (1895) before White (1940) moved P. guilelmiimperatoris to its own genus.

facts.statement: Seeleyosaurus was a relatively small plesiosaur measuring between 2.88 and 3.66 meters long and weighing 199 kilograms.
facts.quote: Seeleyosaurus was a relatively small plesiosaur, measuring 2.88 - 3.66 m long and weighing 199 kg.

facts.statement: A 2025 study by Sachs et al. interpreted Plesiopterys wildi as a distinct taxon from Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris.
facts.quote: A redescription and a study on the affinities of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris published by Sachs et al. (2025) interpreted Plesiopterys wildi as a taxon distinct from S. guilelmiimperatoris.

facts.statement: Seeleyosaurus lived during the Toarcian stage, approximately 184.2 to 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Seeleyosaurus is classified within the family Microcleididae.

rejected.statement: A cast of the holotype revealed an impression of a rhomboidal flap of skin in a vertical plane, suggesting similar skin structures may have existed in other plesiosaurs.
rejected.quote: It preserved soft tissue that was painted over around ten years later and a cast of the holotype was described in by Ketchum & Benson (2011), who determined that it seems to preserve the impression of a rhomboidal flap of skin in a vertical plane, suggesting that many other plesiosaurs may have been equipped in this way.
